evaluation_raw.prompt:
Compare the before and after garment images after one robot handling action. Evaluate the action stage by stage instead of collapsing it into one useful flag. Use only directly visible evidence from the labelled RGB/depth files and the rollout video contact sheets listed at the end. Do not use or search for any other files, including perception JSON, metrics JSON, NumPy arrays, heatmaps, overlays, or MP4 files. The before/after views are static. When chronological rollout contact sheets are supplied, use them to assess acquisition, transport, and laydown over time; otherwise mark those stages UNKNOWN when jaw motion or layer identity cannot actually be established. Never infer success only because the commanded action should have produced it. When a height ridge or sharp relief is present, distinguish two hypotheses: (a) a separable overlapping layer, which should form a visible tent or hanging patch while far garment landmarks remain on the table, versus (b) a rolled wrinkle or local curl, which may only become taller, narrower, or more tightly curled when pulled. Height or gradient alone does not support target_structure_acquired. If the hold frame shows no independent hanging material, or shows the ridge tightening without footprint extension, mark the target structure contradicted/unknown and treat the lateral pull as untested. When a compression probe is visible, compare the selected peak with the immediately adjacent cloth during closure: if the peak-to-neighbour height difference clearly decreases, but no independent hanging patch appears and distant landmarks stay put, classify the event as `COMPRESSIBLE_SINGLE_PEAK`/rolled wrinkle, lower graspability confidence, and do not credit target-layer acquisition. If far landmarks move with the gripper, classify it as whole-garment drag rather than successful ply isolation. Judge progress toward the exact user objective: Fold the shirt into the five ordered steps and a neat compact stack.. Treat that objective as authoritative. Do not declare progress merely because the garment became more open or spread unless that change directly advances the named task. Use the target-selection, target-structure, transport, and laydown fields to record whether the named target was actually manipulated and reached the requested state. Do not invent numeric measurements. For visible_area_delta, overlap_delta, and relief_delta, use INCREASED, DECREASED, UNCHANGED, or UNKNOWN unless an exact numeric measurement is explicitly supplied.

The keep/change decision is mandatory and causal. Put every parameter or strategy that the evidence supports under keep. Put only the earliest failing/unsupported choice and necessary downstream choices under change. Do not change a supported grasp anchor or grasp depth merely because transport failed. For example, when acquisition and target-layer motion are supported but transport is insufficient, keep grasp_anchor and grasp_depth, and change pull_direction and/or pull_distance. When acquisition fails, treat contact location, jaw alignment, pre-close entry path, closure geometry, and Z as competing causal hypotheses. Do not recommend another height-only retry merely because the cloth is thin unless the visible evidence specifically isolates height as the cause. After repeated empty closes with the same contact geometry, next_experiment.change must include at least one non-height contact dimension. Do not name a privileged solution in advance; infer the next hypothesis from the observed failures. The change list must be non-empty when another safe grounded experiment exists. Use an empty change list only when the garment is already as open as this setup can reasonably achieve, or continuing is unsafe, visually ungrounded, or blocked by a hard physical/infrastructure condition.

Optionally propose one skill_update only when the completed before/after evidence supports reusable procedural knowledge. Use operation=create for a genuinely new pattern, or operation=modify for a real change to an existing skill. The guidance must remain high-level and must not contain coordinates, SDK calls, joint angles, or executable code. The skill name must be lowercase kebab-case with hyphens only, for example `grasp-acquisition-check`; never use underscores, spaces, or CamelCase. A proposal is not activated automatically: an independent reviewer checks safety, evidence, and duplicate skills before activation. Omit skill_update when the result only changes this one experiment.

Approved procedural skill library for duplicate checking:
### Skill: collar-full-shake (v1)
Purpose: Use a validated shirt-collar grasp to lift, shake open, transport, and lay the garment down so the collar structure can reveal the garment.
Guidance:
Use only after the visual collar decision and grounded Camera A grasp are validated. Keep the collar grasp orientation fixed and perpendicular to the collar. Lift to a controller-reachable high pose, center at Y=0, perform the host-owned shake-open maneuver, then move toward a useful +X location before retreating toward -X while descending through several waypoints. Keep descent and retreat balanced rather than making either one dominate, release only near the table after the garment has had room to spread, and retract/home afterward. Use current measured geometry and controller IK; never copy fixed coordinates, release in mid-air, or replace the collar with a shoulder or sleeve.

### Skill: controller-ik-recovery (v1)
Purpose: Recover safely when controller IK rejects a garment manipulation path before physical execution.
Guidance:
When controller IK rejects a pose or interpolated segment, preserve the supported visual objective but shorten extreme reach, lift, or transport; keep every waypoint inside the workspace, include a controlled release, and rerun preflight and controller IK before execution.

### Skill: direct-shake (v1)
Purpose: Test whether a validated garment grasp can open the cloth by lifting and shaking it without running the collar-specific transport and laydown routine.
Guidance:
Use after any grounded fabric grasp when the immediate experiment is only a shake response test. Lift to a controller-reachable high pose, keep the held fabric clear of the table, center if useful, run the host-owned shake maneuver, observe whether the garment separates or reveals structure, then lower and release in a controlled way. Do not add a long +X retreat or pretend that a shake-only result proves collar identity; preserve workspace, grounding, preflight, and IK checks and never use fixed coordinates.

### Skill: flatten-garment (v1)
Purpose: Progressively open and flatten a garment by validating the grasped structure, establishing a useful hanging configuration, transporting in a verified opening direction, and laying down only while the scene shows measurable improvement.
Guidance:
Follow this staged workflow:
1. Acquire a validated garment structure: choose a visible, liftable anchor whose local RGB-D measurement, height, and depth consistency support a real garment grasp; do not proceed from an unsupported or table-only point.
2. Establish a hanging configuration if useful: lift to a validated safe height and confirm that the grasped fabric is supported and can hang without dragging or colliding. If the lift does not reveal a supported structure, stop and re-plan.
3. Transport toward a verified opening direction: infer the direction from the current garment geometry and before/after evidence, then use validated intermediate waypoints with stable orientation and workspace margin. The farthest safe X direction is allowed only when the scene verifies that it opens the garment; do not assume it is always correct.
4. Continue only while overlap decreases or coverage increases: after each meaningful transport segment, compare the garment footprint, visible area, layer overlap, and height relief. Stop, release, or re-plan when the move is not improving those measures; never continue a blind pull.
5. Lay down progressively: retreat while descending through validated intermediate heights, release quasi-statically on a clean surface, and avoid dropping, flinging, twisting, or dragging the loaded gripper. The skill supplies this decision sequence, never fixed coordinates or robot API calls.

### Skill: grounding-plan-recovery (v1)
Purpose: Recover from an invalid or inconsistent grounded garment proposal before motion.
Guidance:
When grounding validation rejects a selected point or its use in the plan, reinspect the current evidence, choose a newly grounded visible fabric point, keep the path inside the workspace, include a controlled release, and rerun preflight and IK before execution.

### Skill: hold-checkpoint-timeout-recovery (v1)
Purpose: Interpret and recover from a garment run whose post-grasp hold verification could not be classified in time and therefore forced a local release, and recognize when 15 consecutive acquisition failures across diverse anchor classes with adequate depth definitively disprove single-anchor separation for a configuration and require infrastructure escalation.
Guidance:
Keep the existing rules: a failed-closed or timed-out hold check makes the observation evidence about the grasp only, the unexecuted transport must never be recorded as wrong in direction or distance, and the validated approach clearance, deposit region and quasi-static release carry over to the retry. Add this definitive escalation threshold with infrastructure acknowledgment: when a configuration has produced 15 or more consecutive acquisition failures across at least 5 geometrically distinct anchor classes (peaks, boundary bands, low-relief structures, raised rims, corners, raised edges, claimed free boundary lips) where adequate engagement depth was achieved (closure commanded at or below measured surface height, including compression-probe-recommended depths for high-relief structures and manual calculation for low-relief structures) and every attempt confirms no independent hanging material with all far landmarks remaining seated and hold checkpoint returning FAILED_CLOSED or timeout, treat this as definitive evidence that the garment configuration does not provide separable single-anchor structure. At that threshold, escalate to a two-contact strategy where one contact immobilizes a region through weight, pinning, or clamping while the second contact attempts separation, or target a mechanically verified free edge where the gripper can wrap around a confirmed fabric boundary with visible interior passage or light between plies on both sides. The critical insight: when high-relief structures (17+mm raised edges), medium-relief ridges (10+mm), low-relief corners (sub-4mm and 7mm range), raised plateau tents, compressed peaks, and claimed free boundary lips with adequate depth and varied entry axes (vertical, oblique, side) all produce identical empty-jaws outcomes, the anchor class variety itself and the entry axis variety have both been exhausted. State the infrastructure limitation explicitly when available primitives cannot execute true two-contact opposition: acknowledge that continuing single-anchor attempts is unsafe and ungrounded, and that no further safe grounded experiment is possible within current primitive constraints rather than attempting a 16th single-anchor variant. Preserve validated approach clearance, deposit region, planned pull direction and quasi-static release across the strategy change, since unexecuted transport carries no evidence about those choices.

### Skill: laydown (v2)
Purpose: Convert a garment held from a useful lifting anchor into a more spread tabletop configuration, and recognise when a release has re-piled the garment onto itself instead of opening it.
Guidance:
Keep the quasi-static procedure: let the garment hang under gravity, retreat away from the hanging cloth while descending through intermediate heights, let the hanging face become the upward face, and release in a controlled way. Add two checks. First, before descending, require the retreat to carry the grasp point beyond the horizontal extent of the material still hanging below it, onto clear table, so the fabric unrolls onto bare surface rather than settling back over the area it came from; a retreat shorter than the hanging garment's own reach should be treated as not ready for release. Second, after release, compare footprints rather than only position: if the deposited outline sits inside the previous outline, if previously exposed features such as prints, collars or hems have become covered, and if new steep fold walls appear in depth, judge the laydown a regression caused by too short a retreat, and plan the next deposit farther out across clean table instead of repeating the same descent from the same anchor.

### Skill: molmo-annotation-retry (v1)
Purpose: Recover from an auxiliary Molmo annotation worker failure before motion.
Guidance:
When auxiliary Molmo annotation fails before execution, preserve the saved perception evidence, retry the annotation on a fresh iteration, and never treat a missing semantic anchor as garment-state evidence; keep workspace, release, preflight, and IK validation mandatory before any later motion.

### Skill: null-change-missed-grasp-recovery (v7)
Purpose: Recognise a near-null garment action, separate a clean miss from a contact-without-hold on a compressible pile, and additionally reject a closure whose resolved anchor or engaged height is inconsistent with the visually chosen structure.
Guidance:
Keep the existing null-change and contact-without-hold checks and the escalation rule. Add a pre-closure consistency gate. Before the jaws close, confirm that the anchor the controller actually resolved corresponds to the structure that was chosen in the images, and that the engaged height falls inside the measured relief of that structure rather than collapsing onto the table plane. If the resolved contact point sits far from the visually selected feature, or if the engaged height is indistinguishable from the surrounding tabletop, treat the planned bite as ungrounded and re-ground before descending instead of executing it. Likewise, a local surface measurement taken at a different location, outside the working region, or on bare table is not grounding for the anchor and must not be used to justify a closure. When the resulting observation is a complete null change with every far landmark seated, record it as evidence about the anchor and the engagement geometry only, leave the untested pull direction, pull distance, deposit region and release choices intact, and make the next attempt at a differently structured opening rather than repeating the same descent.

### Skill: planning-timeout-recovery (v1)
Purpose: Recover from a Claude planning timeout before any garment motion starts.
Guidance:
When planning times out before execution, retain the exact failure context, start a fresh planning attempt from saved perception, keep all waypoints inside the workspace, include a controlled release, and rerun preflight and IK before execution.

### Skill: preflight-contract-recovery (v1)
Purpose: Recover from a rejected action schema or unsafe action sequence before motion.
Guidance:
When static preflight rejects a plan, keep only the high-level garment objective, correct the reported action contract or sequence, keep all waypoints inside the workspace, include an explicit release, and rerun preflight and IK before execution.

### Skill: translation-only-reanchor (v22)
Purpose: Recognize when repeated congruent relocations disprove single-anchor peeling for a garment, and additionally retire the terminal end-cap of a rolled bundle as a ply anchor once a perpendicular carry only relocates the whole bundle.
Guidance:
Keep the existing stop rule, the free-boundary verification requirement, and the mandatory lift-phase abort. Add this appearance lesson: the rounded end of an elongated cloth roll, even when it presents solid measurable relief above the table and reads as an end-of-structure boundary with a visible tuck, is not evidence of a separable ply. A roll end is continuous with the body, so carrying it across the table perpendicular to the roll axis relocates the whole bundle instead of paying wound fabric out, and the distal lobe travels with the gripper rather than staying seated. Treat such an outcome as two separate findings: the grounding, engagement depth, approach clearance, fixed wrist orientation and quasi-static release are validated because cloth was held and carried and must be reused unchanged, while the terminal end-cap joins the retired anchor classes alongside the high-relief core, the planar raised shelf, the flat perimeter lip and the steep fold wall. Do not re-tune pull direction or pull distance after such a result, since no layer was isolated and the carry tested nothing. Require either a mechanically verified free fabric boundary with visible interior passage between plies, or opposition supplied by immobilizing material well away from the separation point, before the next lift. Also treat a deposit that lands back over a feature the previous view had exposed as an unhelpful laydown, and place the next deposit farther out on clear surface.

skill_update.name: sleeve-hem-pinch-thin-knit
skill_update.purpose: Reliably acquire a single-layer sleeve hem on a thin knit garment lying flat on a hard table, and detect a failed pinch before committing to transport.
skill_update.guidance: Locate the hem as the elevated band in the height map, then move the grasp point 10-15 mm inboard from the extreme edge so the jaw bites the doubled hem seam rather than a single free edge. Align the jaw perpendicular to the local edge tangent. Descend to 2-3 mm below the detected cloth surface with a compliant press so the fabric is pinned against the table before closing, since a hem lying flush leaves no gap for the finger to slide under. After closing, lift to roughly 30 mm and verify capture with a depth tent test over the grasp neighbourhood; if no local relief appears, abort and re-approach rather than continuing the transport.
skill_update.rationale: This iteration executed a complete close-lift-lower-open cycle with zero net change in the garment, indicating the jaws closed without catching fabric. The failure mode is contact and verification, not target selection, so the skill needs press depth, an inboard doubled-layer bite, and an early abort check.

evaluation_raw.prompt:
Compare the before and after garment images after one robot handling action. Evaluate the action stage by stage instead of collapsing it into one useful flag. Use only directly visible evidence from the labelled RGB/depth files and the rollout video contact sheets listed at the end. Do not use or search for any other files, including perception JSON, metrics JSON, NumPy arrays, heatmaps, overlays, or MP4 files. The before/after views are static. When chronological rollout contact sheets are supplied, use them to assess acquisition, transport, and laydown over time; otherwise mark those stages UNKNOWN when jaw motion or layer identity cannot actually be established. Never infer success only because the commanded action should have produced it. When a height ridge or sharp relief is present, distinguish two hypotheses: (a) a separable overlapping layer, which should form a visible tent or hanging patch while far garment landmarks remain on the table, versus (b) a rolled wrinkle or local curl, which may only become taller, narrower, or more tightly curled when pulled. Height or gradient alone does not support target_structure_acquired. If the hold frame shows no independent hanging material, or shows the ridge tightening without footprint extension, mark the target structure contradicted/unknown and treat the lateral pull as untested. When a compression probe is visible, compare the selected peak with the immediately adjacent cloth during closure: if the peak-to-neighbour height difference clearly decreases, but no independent hanging patch appears and distant landmarks stay put, classify the event as `COMPRESSIBLE_SINGLE_PEAK`/rolled wrinkle, lower graspability confidence, and do not credit target-layer acquisition. If far landmarks move with the gripper, classify it as whole-garment drag rather than successful ply isolation. Judge progress toward the exact user objective: This iteration intentionally tested grasp acquisition only with two short lift checkpoints followed by the reverse path and release at the original contact. Judge whether cloth followed the gripper from the chronological video. Do not expect or credit fold transport or a changed after image; task progress may remain NEUTRAL even when acquisition succeeds.. Treat that objective as authoritative. Do not declare progress merely because the garment became more open or spread unless that change directly advances the named task. Use the target-selection, target-structure, transport, and laydown fields to record whether the named target was actually manipulated and reached the requested state. Do not invent numeric measurements. For visible_area_delta, overlap_delta, and relief_delta, use INCREASED, DECREASED, UNCHANGED, or UNKNOWN unless an exact numeric measurement is explicitly supplied.

The keep/change decision is mandatory and causal. Put every parameter or strategy that the evidence supports under keep. Put only the earliest failing/unsupported choice and necessary downstream choices under change. Do not change a supported grasp anchor or grasp depth merely because transport failed. For example, when acquisition and target-layer motion are supported but transport is insufficient, keep grasp_anchor and grasp_depth, and change pull_direction and/or pull_distance. When acquisition fails, treat contact location, jaw alignment, pre-close entry path, closure geometry, and Z as competing causal hypotheses. Do not recommend another height-only retry merely because the cloth is thin unless the visible evidence specifically isolates height as the cause. After repeated empty closes with the same contact geometry, next_experiment.change must include at least one non-height contact dimension. Do not name a privileged solution in advance; infer the next hypothesis from the observed failures. The change list must be non-empty when another safe grounded experiment exists. Use an empty change list only when the garment is already as open as this setup can reasonably achieve, or continuing is unsafe, visually ungrounded, or blocked by a hard physical/infrastructure condition.

Optionally propose one skill_update only when the completed before/after evidence supports reusable procedural knowledge. Use operation=create for a genuinely new pattern, or operation=modify for a real change to an existing skill. The guidance must remain high-level and must not contain coordinates, SDK calls, joint angles, or executable code. The skill name must be lowercase kebab-case with hyphens only, for example `grasp-acquisition-check`; never use underscores, spaces, or CamelCase. A proposal is not activated automatically: an independent reviewer checks safety, evidence, and duplicate skills before activation. Omit skill_update when the result only changes this one experiment.

Approved procedural skill library for duplicate checking:
### Skill: collar-full-shake (v1)
Purpose: Use a validated shirt-collar grasp to lift, shake open, transport, and lay the garment down so the collar structure can reveal the garment.
Guidance:
Use only after the visual collar decision and grounded Camera A grasp are validated. Keep the collar grasp orientation fixed and perpendicular to the collar. Lift to a controller-reachable high pose, center at Y=0, perform the host-owned shake-open maneuver, then move toward a useful +X location before retreating toward -X while descending through several waypoints. Keep descent and retreat balanced rather than making either one dominate, release only near the table after the garment has had room to spread, and retract/home afterward. Use current measured geometry and controller IK; never copy fixed coordinates, release in mid-air, or replace the collar with a shoulder or sleeve.

### Skill: controller-ik-recovery (v1)
Purpose: Recover safely when controller IK rejects a garment manipulation path before physical execution.
Guidance:
When controller IK rejects a pose or interpolated segment, preserve the supported visual objective but shorten extreme reach, lift, or transport; keep every waypoint inside the workspace, include a controlled release, and rerun preflight and controller IK before execution.

### Skill: direct-shake (v1)
Purpose: Test whether a validated garment grasp can open the cloth by lifting and shaking it without running the collar-specific transport and laydown routine.
Guidance:
Use after any grounded fabric grasp when the immediate experiment is only a shake response test. Lift to a controller-reachable high pose, keep the held fabric clear of the table, center if useful, run the host-owned shake maneuver, observe whether the garment separates or reveals structure, then lower and release in a controlled way. Do not add a long +X retreat or pretend that a shake-only result proves collar identity; preserve workspace, grounding, preflight, and IK checks and never use fixed coordinates.

### Skill: flatten-garment (v1)
Purpose: Progressively open and flatten a garment by validating the grasped structure, establishing a useful hanging configuration, transporting in a verified opening direction, and laying down only while the scene shows measurable improvement.
Guidance:
Follow this staged workflow:
1. Acquire a validated garment structure: choose a visible, liftable anchor whose local RGB-D measurement, height, and depth consistency support a real garment grasp; do not proceed from an unsupported or table-only point.
2. Establish a hanging configuration if useful: lift to a validated safe height and confirm that the grasped fabric is supported and can hang without dragging or colliding. If the lift does not reveal a supported structure, stop and re-plan.
3. Transport toward a verified opening direction: infer the direction from the current garment geometry and before/after evidence, then use validated intermediate waypoints with stable orientation and workspace margin. The farthest safe X direction is allowed only when the scene verifies that it opens the garment; do not assume it is always correct.
4. Continue only while overlap decreases or coverage increases: after each meaningful transport segment, compare the garment footprint, visible area, layer overlap, and height relief. Stop, release, or re-plan when the move is not improving those measures; never continue a blind pull.
5. Lay down progressively: retreat while descending through validated intermediate heights, release quasi-statically on a clean surface, and avoid dropping, flinging, twisting, or dragging the loaded gripper. The skill supplies this decision sequence, never fixed coordinates or robot API calls.

### Skill: grounding-plan-recovery (v1)
Purpose: Recover from an invalid or inconsistent grounded garment proposal before motion.
Guidance:
When grounding validation rejects a selected point or its use in the plan, reinspect the current evidence, choose a newly grounded visible fabric point, keep the path inside the workspace, include a controlled release, and rerun preflight and IK before execution.

### Skill: hold-checkpoint-timeout-recovery (v1)
Purpose: Interpret and recover from a garment run whose post-grasp hold verification could not be classified in time and therefore forced a local release, and recognize when 15 consecutive acquisition failures across diverse anchor classes with adequate depth definitively disprove single-anchor separation for a configuration and require infrastructure escalation.
Guidance:
Keep the existing rules: a failed-closed or timed-out hold check makes the observation evidence about the grasp only, the unexecuted transport must never be recorded as wrong in direction or distance, and the validated approach clearance, deposit region and quasi-static release carry over to the retry. Add this definitive escalation threshold with infrastructure acknowledgment: when a configuration has produced 15 or more consecutive acquisition failures across at least 5 geometrically distinct anchor classes (peaks, boundary bands, low-relief structures, raised rims, corners, raised edges, claimed free boundary lips) where adequate engagement depth was achieved (closure commanded at or below measured surface height, including compression-probe-recommended depths for high-relief structures and manual calculation for low-relief structures) and every attempt confirms no independent hanging material with all far landmarks remaining seated and hold checkpoint returning FAILED_CLOSED or timeout, treat this as definitive evidence that the garment configuration does not provide separable single-anchor structure. At that threshold, escalate to a two-contact strategy where one contact immobilizes a region through weight, pinning, or clamping while the second contact attempts separation, or target a mechanically verified free edge where the gripper can wrap around a confirmed fabric boundary with visible interior passage or light between plies on both sides. The critical insight: when high-relief structures (17+mm raised edges), medium-relief ridges (10+mm), low-relief corners (sub-4mm and 7mm range), raised plateau tents, compressed peaks, and claimed free boundary lips with adequate depth and varied entry axes (vertical, oblique, side) all produce identical empty-jaws outcomes, the anchor class variety itself and the entry axis variety have both been exhausted. State the infrastructure limitation explicitly when available primitives cannot execute true two-contact opposition: acknowledge that continuing single-anchor attempts is unsafe and ungrounded, and that no further safe grounded experiment is possible within current primitive constraints rather than attempting a 16th single-anchor variant. Preserve validated approach clearance, deposit region, planned pull direction and quasi-static release across the strategy change, since unexecuted transport carries no evidence about those choices.

### Skill: laydown (v2)
Purpose: Convert a garment held from a useful lifting anchor into a more spread tabletop configuration, and recognise when a release has re-piled the garment onto itself instead of opening it.
Guidance:
Keep the quasi-static procedure: let the garment hang under gravity, retreat away from the hanging cloth while descending through intermediate heights, let the hanging face become the upward face, and release in a controlled way. Add two checks. First, before descending, require the retreat to carry the grasp point beyond the horizontal extent of the material still hanging below it, onto clear table, so the fabric unrolls onto bare surface rather than settling back over the area it came from; a retreat shorter than the hanging garment's own reach should be treated as not ready for release. Second, after release, compare footprints rather than only position: if the deposited outline sits inside the previous outline, if previously exposed features such as prints, collars or hems have become covered, and if new steep fold walls appear in depth, judge the laydown a regression caused by too short a retreat, and plan the next deposit farther out across clean table instead of repeating the same descent from the same anchor.

### Skill: molmo-annotation-retry (v1)
Purpose: Recover from an auxiliary Molmo annotation worker failure before motion.
Guidance:
When auxiliary Molmo annotation fails before execution, preserve the saved perception evidence, retry the annotation on a fresh iteration, and never treat a missing semantic anchor as garment-state evidence; keep workspace, release, preflight, and IK validation mandatory before any later motion.

### Skill: null-change-missed-grasp-recovery (v7)
Purpose: Recognise a near-null garment action, separate a clean miss from a contact-without-hold on a compressible pile, and additionally reject a closure whose resolved anchor or engaged height is inconsistent with the visually chosen structure.
Guidance:
Keep the existing null-change and contact-without-hold checks and the escalation rule. Add a pre-closure consistency gate. Before the jaws close, confirm that the anchor the controller actually resolved corresponds to the structure that was chosen in the images, and that the engaged height falls inside the measured relief of that structure rather than collapsing onto the table plane. If the resolved contact point sits far from the visually selected feature, or if the engaged height is indistinguishable from the surrounding tabletop, treat the planned bite as ungrounded and re-ground before descending instead of executing it. Likewise, a local surface measurement taken at a different location, outside the working region, or on bare table is not grounding for the anchor and must not be used to justify a closure. When the resulting observation is a complete null change with every far landmark seated, record it as evidence about the anchor and the engagement geometry only, leave the untested pull direction, pull distance, deposit region and release choices intact, and make the next attempt at a differently structured opening rather than repeating the same descent.

### Skill: planning-timeout-recovery (v1)
Purpose: Recover from a Claude planning timeout before any garment motion starts.
Guidance:
When planning times out before execution, retain the exact failure context, start a fresh planning attempt from saved perception, keep all waypoints inside the workspace, include a controlled release, and rerun preflight and IK before execution.

### Skill: preflight-contract-recovery (v1)
Purpose: Recover from a rejected action schema or unsafe action sequence before motion.
Guidance:
When static preflight rejects a plan, keep only the high-level garment objective, correct the reported action contract or sequence, keep all waypoints inside the workspace, include an explicit release, and rerun preflight and IK before execution.

### Skill: translation-only-reanchor (v22)
Purpose: Recognize when repeated congruent relocations disprove single-anchor peeling for a garment, and additionally retire the terminal end-cap of a rolled bundle as a ply anchor once a perpendicular carry only relocates the whole bundle.
Guidance:
Keep the existing stop rule, the free-boundary verification requirement, and the mandatory lift-phase abort. Add this appearance lesson: the rounded end of an elongated cloth roll, even when it presents solid measurable relief above the table and reads as an end-of-structure boundary with a visible tuck, is not evidence of a separable ply. A roll end is continuous with the body, so carrying it across the table perpendicular to the roll axis relocates the whole bundle instead of paying wound fabric out, and the distal lobe travels with the gripper rather than staying seated. Treat such an outcome as two separate findings: the grounding, engagement depth, approach clearance, fixed wrist orientation and quasi-static release are validated because cloth was held and carried and must be reused unchanged, while the terminal end-cap joins the retired anchor classes alongside the high-relief core, the planar raised shelf, the flat perimeter lip and the steep fold wall. Do not re-tune pull direction or pull distance after such a result, since no layer was isolated and the carry tested nothing. Require either a mechanically verified free fabric boundary with visible interior passage between plies, or opposition supplied by immobilizing material well away from the separation point, before the next lift. Also treat a deposit that lands back over a feature the previous view had exposed as an unhelpful laydown, and place the next deposit farther out on clear surface.

### Skill: collar-full-shake (v1)
Purpose: Use a validated shirt-collar grasp to lift, shake open, transport, and lay the garment down so the collar structure can reveal the garment.
Guidance:
Use only after the visual collar decision and grounded Camera A grasp are validated. Keep the collar grasp orientation fixed and perpendicular to the collar. Lift to a controller-reachable high pose, center at Y=0, perform the host-owned shake-open maneuver, then move toward a useful +X location before retreating toward -X while descending through several waypoints. Keep descent and retreat balanced rather than making either one dominate, release only near the table after the garment has had room to spread, and retract/home afterward. Use current measured geometry and controller IK; never copy fixed coordinates, release in mid-air, or replace the collar with a shoulder or sleeve.

### Skill: controller-ik-recovery (v1)
Purpose: Recover safely when controller IK rejects a garment manipulation path before physical execution.
Guidance:
When controller IK rejects a pose or interpolated segment, preserve the supported visual objective but shorten extreme reach, lift, or transport; keep every waypoint inside the workspace, include a controlled release, and rerun preflight and controller IK before execution.

### Skill: direct-shake (v1)
Purpose: Test whether a validated garment grasp can open the cloth by lifting and shaking it without running the collar-specific transport and laydown routine.
Guidance:

Lift to a controller-reachable high pose, keep the held fabric clear of the table, center if useful, run the host-owned shake maneuver, observe whether the garment separates or reveals structure, then lower and release in a controlled way. Do not add a long +X retreat or pretend that a shake-only result proves collar identity; preserve workspace, grounding, preflight, and IK checks and never use fixed coordinates.

### Skill: flatten-garment (v1)
Purpose: Progressively open and flatten a garment by validating the grasped structure, establishing a useful hanging configuration, transporting in a verified opening direction, and laying down only while the scene shows measurable improvement.
Guidance:
Follow this staged workflow:
1. Acquire a validated garment structure: choose a visible, liftable anchor whose local RGB-D measurement, height, and depth consistency support a real garment grasp; do not proceed from an unsupported or table-only point.
2. Establish a hanging configuration if useful: lift to a validated safe height and confirm that the grasped fabric is supported and can hang without dragging or colliding. If the lift does not reveal a supported structure, stop and re-plan.
3. Transport toward a verified opening direction: infer the direction from the current garment geometry and before/after evidence, then use validated intermediate waypoints with stable orientation and workspace margin. The farthest safe X direction is allowed only when the scene verifies that it opens the garment; do not assume it is always correct.
4. Continue only while overlap decreases or coverage increases: after each meaningful transport segment, compare the garment footprint, visible area, layer overlap, and height relief. Stop, release, or re-plan when the move is not improving those measures; never continue a blind pull.
5. Lay down progressively: retreat while descending through validated intermediate heights, release quasi-statically on a clean surface, and avoid dropping, flinging, twisting, or dragging the loaded gripper. The skill supplies this decision sequence, never fixed coordinates or robot API calls.

### Skill: grounding-plan-recovery (v1)
Purpose: Recover from an invalid or inconsistent grounded garment proposal before motion.
Guidance:
When grounding validation rejects a selected point or its use in the plan, reinspect the current evidence, choose a newly grounded visible fabric point, keep the path inside the workspace, include a controlled release, and rerun preflight and IK before execution.

### Skill: hold-checkpoint-timeout-recovery (v1)
Purpose: Interpret and recover from a garment run whose post-grasp hold verification could not be classified in time and therefore forced a local release, and recognize when 15 consecutive acquisition failures across diverse anchor classes with adequate depth definitively disprove single-anchor separation for a configuration and require infrastructure escalation.
Guidance:
Keep the existing rules: a failed-closed or timed-out hold check makes the observation evidence about the grasp only, the unexecuted transport must never be recorded as wrong in direction or distance, and the validated approach clearance, deposit region and quasi-static release carry over to the retry. Add this definitive escalation threshold with infrastructure acknowledgment: when a configuration has produced 15 or more consecutive acquisition failures across at least 5 geometrically distinct anchor classes (peaks, boundary bands, low-relief structures, raised rims, corners, raised edges, claimed free boundary lips) where adequate engagement depth was achieved (closure commanded at or below measured surface height, including compression-probe-recommended depths for high-relief structures and manual calculation for low-relief structures) and every attempt confirms no independent hanging material with all far landmarks remaining seated and hold checkpoint returning FAILED_CLOSED or timeout, treat this as definitive evidence that the garment configuration does not provide separable single-anchor structure. At that threshold, escalate to a two-contact strategy where one contact immobilizes a region through weight, pinning, or clamping while the second contact attempts separation, or target a mechanically verified free edge where the gripper can wrap around a confirmed fabric boundary with visible interior passage or light between plies on both sides. The critical insight: when high-relief structures (17+mm raised edges), medium-relief ridges (10+mm), low-relief corners (sub-4mm and 7mm range), raised plateau tents, compressed peaks, and claimed free boundary lips with adequate depth and varied entry axes (vertical, oblique, side) all produce identical empty-jaws outcomes, the anchor class variety itself and the entry axis variety have both been exhausted. State the infrastructure limitation explicitly when available primitives cannot execute true two-contact opposition: acknowledge that continuing single-anchor attempts is unsafe and ungrounded, and that no further safe grounded experiment is possible within current primitive constraints rather than attempting a 16th single-anchor variant. Preserve validated approach clearance, deposit region, planned pull direction and quasi-static release across the strategy change, since unexecuted transport carries no evidence about those choices.

### Skill: laydown (v2)
Purpose: Convert a garment held from a useful lifting anchor into a more spread tabletop configuration, and recognise when a release has re-piled the garment onto itself instead of opening it.
Guidance:
Keep the quasi-static procedure: let the garment hang under gravity, retreat away from the hanging cloth while descending through intermediate heights, let the hanging face become the upward face, and release in a controlled way. Add two checks. First, before descending, require the retreat to carry the grasp point beyond the horizontal extent of the material still hanging below it, onto clear table, so the fabric unrolls onto bare surface rather than settling back over the area it came from; a retreat shorter than the hanging garment's own reach should be treated as not ready for release. Second, after release, compare footprints rather than only position: if the deposited outline sits inside the previous outline, if previously exposed features such as prints, collars or hems have become covered, and if new steep fold walls appear in depth, judge the laydown a regression caused by too short a retreat, and plan the next deposit farther out across clean table instead of repeating the same descent from the same anchor.

skill_update.name: sleeve-hem-pinch-thin-knit
skill_update.purpose: Reliably acquire a single-layer sleeve hem on a thin knit garment lying flat on a hard table, and detect a failed pinch before committing to transport.
skill_update.guidance: Locate the hem as the elevated band in the height map, then move the grasp point 10-15 mm inboard from the extreme edge so the jaw bites the doubled hem seam rather than a single free edge. Align the jaw perpendicular to the local edge tangent. Descend to 2-3 mm below the detected cloth surface with a compliant press so the fabric is pinned against the table before closing, since a hem lying flush leaves no gap for the finger to slide under. After closing, lift to roughly 30 mm and verify capture with a depth tent test over the grasp neighbourhood; if no local relief appears, abort and re-approach rather than continuing the transport.
skill_update.rationale: This iteration executed a complete close-lift-lower-open cycle with zero net change in the garment, indicating the jaws closed without catching fabric. The failure mode is contact and verification, not target selection, so the skill needs press depth, an inboard doubled-layer bite, and an early abort check.

safety_notes: Single-step reversible probe only: one grasp, one short inward drag, one laydown. Do not chain into later fold steps (right sleeve, torso sides, hem) in this iteration.

Verify acquisition by cloth tenting in Camera A at a low intermediate lift before any transport; abort and retreat straight up if no cloth is detected, so an empty jaw is never dragged across the garment.
Limit the compliant press to a few millimetres past the detected cloth surface. Do not solve a null grasp by pressing harder into the table, which risks fingertip and table contact loading.
Keep the oblique entry outside the silhouette until the fingertip is under the hem lip, so the approach never scuffs or drags the chest print or the neck label.

Keep transport short and inboard along the sleeve axis; avoid pulling the garment toward the bottom frame border, where the Camera A mask already touches the edge with an 8 px margin and further motion would clip observability.
Do not rely on Camera B for closure or lift verification: it was fully occluded through the decisive window in the previous attempt.
Release quasi-statically with stationary jaws and retreat vertically, so the deposited sleeve is not dragged back out of position.
Treat the magenta MOLMO point as a fallible region hint only; never command a grasp at it directly.
If a third consecutive null acquisition occurs, stop repeating the edge-bite family and report the mechanics failure rather than escalating force or grasp depth.

### Skill: collar-full-shake (v1)
Purpose: Use a validated shirt-collar grasp to lift, shake open, transport, and lay the garment down so the collar structure can reveal the garment.
Guidance:
Use only after the visual collar decision and grounded Camera A grasp are validated. Keep the collar grasp orientation fixed and perpendicular to the collar. Lift to a controller-reachable high pose, center at Y=0, perform the host-owned shake-open maneuver, then move toward a useful +X location before retreating toward -X while descending through several waypoints. Keep descent and retreat balanced rather than making either one dominate, release only near the table after the garment has had room to spread, and retract/home afterward. Use current measured geometry and controller IK; never copy fixed coordinates, release in mid-air, or replace the collar with a shoulder or sleeve.

### Skill: controller-ik-recovery (v1)
Purpose: Recover safely when controller IK rejects a garment manipulation path before physical execution.
Guidance:
When controller IK rejects a pose or interpolated segment, preserve the supported visual objective but shorten extreme reach, lift, or transport; keep every waypoint inside the workspace, include a controlled release, and rerun preflight and controller IK before execution.

### Skill: direct-shake (v1)
Purpose: Test whether a validated garment grasp can open the cloth by lifting and shaking it without running the collar-specific transport and laydown routine.
Guidance:
Use after any grounded fabric grasp when the immediate experiment is only a shake response test. Lift to a controller-reachable high pose, keep the held fabric clear of the table, center if useful, run the host-owned shake maneuver, observe whether the garment separates or reveals structure, then lower and release in a controlled way. Do not add a long +X retreat or pretend that a shake-only result proves collar identity; preserve workspace, grounding, preflight, and IK checks and never use fixed coordinates.

### Skill: flatten-garment (v1)
Purpose: Progressively open and flatten a garment by validating the grasped structure, establishing a useful hanging configuration, transporting in a verified opening direction, and laying down only while the scene shows measurable improvement.
Guidance:
Follow this staged workflow:
1. Acquire a validated garment structure: choose a visible, liftable anchor whose local RGB-D measurement, height, and depth consistency support a real garment grasp; do not proceed from an unsupported or table-only point.
2. Establish a hanging configuration if useful: lift to a validated safe height and confirm that the grasped fabric is supported and can hang without dragging or colliding. If the lift does not reveal a supported structure, stop and re-plan.
3. Transport toward a verified opening direction: infer the direction from the current garment geometry and before/after evidence, then use validated intermediate waypoints with stable orientation and workspace margin. The farthest safe X direction is allowed only when the scene verifies that it opens the garment; do not assume it is always correct.
4. Continue only while overlap decreases or coverage increases: after each meaningful transport segment, compare the garment footprint, visible area, layer overlap, and height relief. Stop, release, or re-plan when the move is not improving those measures; never continue a blind pull.
5. Lay down progressively: retreat while descending through validated intermediate heights, release quasi-statically on a clean surface, and avoid dropping, flinging, twisting, or dragging the loaded gripper. The skill supplies this decision sequence, never fixed coordinates or robot API calls.

### Skill: grounding-plan-recovery (v1)
Purpose: Recover from an invalid or inconsistent grounded garment proposal before motion.
Guidance:
When grounding validation rejects a selected point or its use in the plan, reinspect the current evidence, choose a newly grounded visible fabric point, keep the path inside the workspace, include a controlled release, and rerun preflight and IK before execution.

### Skill: hold-checkpoint-timeout-recovery (v1)
Purpose: Interpret and recover from a garment run whose post-grasp hold verification could not be classified in time and therefore forced a local release, and recognize when 15 consecutive acquisition failures across diverse anchor classes with adequate depth definitively disprove single-anchor separation for a configuration and require infrastructure escalation.
Guidance:
Keep the existing rules: a failed-closed or timed-out hold check makes the observation evidence about the grasp only, the unexecuted transport must never be recorded as wrong in direction or distance, and the validated approach clearance, deposit region and quasi-static release carry over to the retry. Add this definitive escalation threshold with infrastructure acknowledgment: when a configuration has produced 15 or more consecutive acquisition failures across at least 5 geometrically distinct anchor classes (peaks, boundary bands, low-relief structures, raised rims, corners, raised edges, claimed free boundary lips) where adequate engagement depth was achieved (closure commanded at or below measured surface height, including compression-probe-recommended depths for high-relief structures and manual calculation for low-relief structures) and every attempt confirms no independent hanging material with all far landmarks remaining seated and hold checkpoint returning FAILED_CLOSED or timeout, treat this as definitive evidence that the garment configuration does not provide separable single-anchor structure. At that threshold, escalate to a two-contact strategy where one contact immobilizes a region through weight, pinning, or clamping while the second contact attempts separation, or target a mechanically verified free edge where the gripper can wrap around a confirmed fabric boundary with visible interior passage or light between plies on both sides. The critical insight: when high-relief structures (17+mm raised edges), medium-relief ridges (10+mm), low-relief corners (sub-4mm and 7mm range), raised plateau tents, compressed peaks, and claimed free boundary lips with adequate depth and varied entry axes (vertical, oblique, side) all produce identical empty-jaws outcomes, the anchor class variety itself and the entry axis variety have both been exhausted. State the infrastructure limitation explicitly when available primitives cannot execute true two-contact opposition: acknowledge that continuing single-anchor attempts is unsafe and ungrounded, and that no further safe grounded experiment is possible within current primitive constraints rather than attempting a 16th single-anchor variant. Preserve validated approach clearance, deposit region, planned pull direction and quasi-static release across the strategy change, since unexecuted transport carries no evidence about those choices.

### Skill: laydown (v2)
Purpose: Convert a garment held from a useful lifting anchor into a more spread tabletop configuration, and recognise when a release has re-piled the garment onto itself instead of opening it.
Guidance:
Keep the quasi-static procedure: let the garment hang under gravity, retreat away from the hanging cloth while descending through intermediate heights, let the hanging face become the upward face, and release in a controlled way. Add two checks. First, before descending, require the retreat to carry the grasp point beyond the horizontal extent of the material still hanging below it, onto clear table, so the fabric unrolls onto bare surface rather than settling back over the area it came from; a retreat shorter than the hanging garment's own reach should be treated as not ready for release. Second, after release, compare footprints rather than only position: if the deposited outline sits inside the previous outline, if previously exposed features such as prints, collars or hems have become covered, and if new steep fold walls appear in depth, judge the laydown a regression caused by too short a retreat, and plan the next deposit farther out across clean table instead of repeating the same descent from the same anchor.

### Skill: molmo-annotation-retry (v1)
Purpose: Recover from an auxiliary Molmo annotation worker failure before motion.
Guidance:
When auxiliary Molmo annotation fails before execution, preserve the saved perception evidence, retry the annotation on a fresh iteration, and never treat a missing semantic anchor as garment-state evidence; keep workspace, release, preflight, and IK validation mandatory before any later motion.

### Skill: null-change-missed-grasp-recovery (v7)
Purpose: Recognise a near-null garment action, separate a clean miss from a contact-without-hold on a compressible pile, and additionally reject a closure whose resolved anchor or engaged height is inconsistent with the visually chosen structure.
Guidance:
Keep the existing null-change and contact-without-hold checks and the escalation rule. Add a pre-closure consistency gate. Before the jaws close, confirm that the anchor the controller actually resolved corresponds to the structure that was chosen in the images, and that the engaged height falls inside the measured relief of that structure rather than collapsing onto the table plane. If the resolved contact point sits far from the visually selected feature, or if the engaged height is indistinguishable from the surrounding tabletop, treat the planned bite as ungrounded and re-ground before descending instead of executing it. Likewise, a local surface measurement taken at a different location, outside the working region, or on bare table is not grounding for the anchor and must not be used to justify a closure. When the resulting observation is a complete null change with every far landmark seated, record it as evidence about the anchor and the engagement geometry only, leave the untested pull direction, pull distance, deposit region and release choices intact, and make the next attempt at a differently structured opening rather than repeating the same descent.

### Skill: planning-timeout-recovery (v1)
Purpose: Recover from a Claude planning timeout before any garment motion starts.
Guidance:
When planning times out before execution, retain the exact failure context, start a fresh planning attempt from saved perception, keep all waypoints inside the workspace, include a controlled release, and rerun preflight and IK before execution.

### Skill: preflight-contract-recovery (v1)
Purpose: Recover from a rejected action schema or unsafe action sequence before motion.
Guidance:
When static preflight rejects a plan, keep only the high-level garment objective, correct the reported action contract or sequence, keep all waypoints inside the workspace, include an explicit release, and rerun preflight and IK before execution.

### Skill: translation-only-reanchor (v22)
Purpose: Recognize when repeated congruent relocations disprove single-anchor peeling for a garment, and additionally retire the terminal end-cap of a rolled bundle as a ply anchor once a perpendicular carry only relocates the whole bundle.
Guidance:
Keep the existing stop rule, the free-boundary verification requirement, and the mandatory lift-phase abort. Add this appearance lesson: the rounded end of an elongated cloth roll, even when it presents solid measurable relief above the table and reads as an end-of-structure boundary with a visible tuck, is not evidence of a separable ply. A roll end is continuous with the body, so carrying it across the table perpendicular to the roll axis relocates the whole bundle instead of paying wound fabric out, and the distal lobe travels with the gripper rather than staying seated. Treat such an outcome as two separate findings: the grounding, engagement depth, approach clearance, fixed wrist orientation and quasi-static release are validated because cloth was held and carried and must be reused unchanged, while the terminal end-cap joins the retired anchor classes alongside the high-relief core, the planar raised shelf, the flat perimeter lip and the steep fold wall. Do not re-tune pull direction or pull distance after such a result, since no layer was isolated and the carry tested nothing. Require either a mechanically verified free fabric boundary with visible interior passage between plies, or opposition supplied by immobilizing material well away from the separation point, before the next lift. Also treat a deposit that lands back over a feature the previous view had exposed as an unhelpful laydown, and place the next deposit farther out on clear surface.

### Skill: collar-full-shake (v1)
Purpose: Use a validated shirt-collar grasp to lift, shake open, transport, and lay the garment down so the collar structure can reveal the garment.
Guidance:
Use only after the visual collar decision and grounded Camera A grasp are validated. Keep the collar grasp orientation fixed and perpendicular to the collar. Lift to a controller-reachable high pose, center at Y=0, perform the host-owned shake-open maneuver, then move toward a useful +X location before retreating toward -X while descending through several waypoints. Keep descent and retreat balanced rather than making either one dominate, release only near the table after the garment has had room to spread, and retract/home afterward. Use current measured geometry and controller IK; never copy fixed coordinates, release in mid-air, or replace the collar with a shoulder or sleeve.

### Skill: controller-ik-recovery (v1)
Purpose: Recover safely when controller IK rejects a garment manipulation path before physical execution.
Guidance:
When controller IK rejects a pose or interpolated segment, preserve the supported visual objective but shorten extreme reach, lift, or transport; keep every waypoint inside the workspace, include a controlled release, and rerun preflight and controller IK before execution.

### Skill: direct-shake (v1)
Purpose: Test whether a validated garment grasp can open the cloth by lifting and shaking it without running the collar-specific transport and laydown routine.
Guidance:

Lift to a controller-reachable high pose, keep the held fabric clear of the table, center if useful, run the host-owned shake maneuver, observe whether the garment separates or reveals structure, then lower and release in a controlled way. Do not add a long +X retreat or pretend that a shake-only result proves collar identity; preserve workspace, grounding, preflight, and IK checks and never use fixed coordinates.

### Skill: flatten-garment (v1)
Purpose: Progressively open and flatten a garment by validating the grasped structure, establishing a useful hanging configuration, transporting in a verified opening direction, and laying down only while the scene shows measurable improvement.
Guidance:
Follow this staged workflow:
1. Acquire a validated garment structure: choose a visible, liftable anchor whose local RGB-D measurement, height, and depth consistency support a real garment grasp; do not proceed from an unsupported or table-only point.
2. Establish a hanging configuration if useful: lift to a validated safe height and confirm that the grasped fabric is supported and can hang without dragging or colliding. If the lift does not reveal a supported structure, stop and re-plan.
3. Transport toward a verified opening direction: infer the direction from the current garment geometry and before/after evidence, then use validated intermediate waypoints with stable orientation and workspace margin. The farthest safe X direction is allowed only when the scene verifies that it opens the garment; do not assume it is always correct.
4. Continue only while overlap decreases or coverage increases: after each meaningful transport segment, compare the garment footprint, visible area, layer overlap, and height relief. Stop, release, or re-plan when the move is not improving those measures; never continue a blind pull.
5. Lay down progressively: retreat while descending through validated intermediate heights, release quasi-statically on a clean surface, and avoid dropping, flinging, twisting, or dragging the loaded gripper. The skill supplies this decision sequence, never fixed coordinates or robot API calls.

### Skill: grounding-plan-recovery (v1)
Purpose: Recover from an invalid or inconsistent grounded garment proposal before motion.
Guidance:
When grounding validation rejects a selected point or its use in the plan, reinspect the current evidence, choose a newly grounded visible fabric point, keep the path inside the workspace, include a controlled release, and rerun preflight and IK before execution.

### Skill: hold-checkpoint-timeout-recovery (v1)
Purpose: Interpret and recover from a garment run whose post-grasp hold verification could not be classified in time and therefore forced a local release, and recognize when 15 consecutive acquisition failures across diverse anchor classes with adequate depth definitively disprove single-anchor separation for a configuration and require infrastructure escalation.
Guidance:
Keep the existing rules: a failed-closed or timed-out hold check makes the observation evidence about the grasp only, the unexecuted transport must never be recorded as wrong in direction or distance, and the validated approach clearance, deposit region and quasi-static release carry over to the retry. Add this definitive escalation threshold with infrastructure acknowledgment: when a configuration has produced 15 or more consecutive acquisition failures across at least 5 geometrically distinct anchor classes (peaks, boundary bands, low-relief structures, raised rims, corners, raised edges, claimed free boundary lips) where adequate engagement depth was achieved (closure commanded at or below measured surface height, including compression-probe-recommended depths for high-relief structures and manual calculation for low-relief structures) and every attempt confirms no independent hanging material with all far landmarks remaining seated and hold checkpoint returning FAILED_CLOSED or timeout, treat this as definitive evidence that the garment configuration does not provide separable single-anchor structure. At that threshold, escalate to a two-contact strategy where one contact immobilizes a region through weight, pinning, or clamping while the second contact attempts separation, or target a mechanically verified free edge where the gripper can wrap around a confirmed fabric boundary with visible interior passage or light between plies on both sides. The critical insight: when high-relief structures (17+mm raised edges), medium-relief ridges (10+mm), low-relief corners (sub-4mm and 7mm range), raised plateau tents, compressed peaks, and claimed free boundary lips with adequate depth and varied entry axes (vertical, oblique, side) all produce identical empty-jaws outcomes, the anchor class variety itself and the entry axis variety have both been exhausted. State the infrastructure limitation explicitly when available primitives cannot execute true two-contact opposition: acknowledge that continuing single-anchor attempts is unsafe and ungrounded, and that no further safe grounded experiment is possible within current primitive constraints rather than attempting a 16th single-anchor variant. Preserve validated approach clearance, deposit region, planned pull direction and quasi-static release across the strategy change, since unexecuted transport carries no evidence about those choices.

### Skill: laydown (v2)
Purpose: Convert a garment held from a useful lifting anchor into a more spread tabletop configuration, and recognise when a release has re-piled the garment onto itself instead of opening it.
Guidance:
Keep the quasi-static procedure: let the garment hang under gravity, retreat away from the hanging cloth while descending through intermediate heights, let the hanging face become the upward face, and release in a controlled way. Add two checks. First, before descending, require the retreat to carry the grasp point beyond the horizontal extent of the material still hanging below it, onto clear table, so the fabric unrolls onto bare surface rather than settling back over the area it came from; a retreat shorter than the hanging garment's own reach should be treated as not ready for release. Second, after release, compare footprints rather than only position: if the deposited outline sits inside the previous outline, if previously exposed features such as prints, collars or hems have become covered, and if new steep fold walls appear in depth, judge the laydown a regression caused by too short a retreat, and plan the next deposit farther out across clean table instead of repeating the same descent from the same anchor.

evidence: Before overlay is labelled LEFT_SLEEVE and places the magenta MOLMO hypothesis marker together with the R092/R094 cyan anchors on garment fabric at the left sleeve region, not on bare table.
Camera A upright RGB confirms a real, unoccluded left sleeve with a visible free cuff boundary against the white table, so the named structure exists and is reachable.

Camera A height heatmap shows the sleeve/shoulder side of the garment as the warmer, higher-relief half, so the selected side does carry measurable relief above the table rather than being pure table plane.

Contact sheet shows the full commanded sequence: gripper enters frame around checkpoint #07-#08, is positioned over the garment through #10-#14, and is clear of the cloth again by #16, so jaw descent, closure and reverse motion did occur.

In no camera A panel of the contact sheet does the sleeve region rise, tent, or deform while the gripper is at the raised checkpoints; the garment outline and the near sleeve boundary stay identical from #01 through #16.
No hanging or supported patch of fabric appears under the jaws in any camera B panel during the lift window; the cloth surface beneath the tool reads flat.

Before/after camera A upright RGB are near identical: print tiles, neck label, shoulder line, both sleeves and hem all in the same place, consistent with jaws that closed on nothing or slipped immediately.
Before/after camera B raw show the same garment pose with only a faint crease difference near the left shoulder/sleeve seam, i.e. surface contact without capture.

Confidence is held at moderate because camera B is largely occluded by the gripper body through the decisive closure window and camera A panels in the contact sheet are low resolution, so a very small held lip cannot be fully excluded.
Neither lift checkpoint shows independent hanging material below the jaws in either view, which is the required signature of an isolated sleeve ply.
All far landmarks stay seated across the whole rollout: neck label, print block, right sleeve and hem hold position in camera A and camera B, so no ply and no whole garment travelled with the tool.

Before/after camera A height heatmaps keep the same footprint and the same warm sleeve region; the only differences are local mottling and small invalid-depth speckles near the left edge, not a new tent or a removed layer.
With empty jaws there is no evidence that the sleeve layer was separated from the panel beneath it, so the sleeve-as-separable-ply hypothesis is unsupported by this run.
The iteration was deliberately acquisition-only: the action program lifts to two checkpoints then retraces the same path and releases at the original contact, with no lateral segment.
The planned 25 mm inboard +Y carry was not part of the executed program, so pull direction and pull distance were never exercised.
Because nothing was held, no cloth motion is available from which to judge direction or distance; transport remains untested rather than wrong.
The gripper opened at the original contact point after the reverse descent, so no deposit onto new surface was attempted.
No fabric was supported at the release moment, so there was no laydown event to judge; the final contact-sheet checkpoint shows the same flat garment as the first.
